prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (keep safety authority). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (DPS, Marlinstone; unconstrained demand); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Slot Allocation Engine (SAE, Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (DMS, Emberline; optional Passenger Misconnect Count). DPS/CAM/SAE/DMS reject data lacking Time Synchronization Service timestamp. Airport CDM Portal; Identity Access Service (IAS); Audit Event Ledger; Alert Distribution Hub (Digital Briefing Room); Performance Analytics Warehouse (delay absorption, adherence, emissions factors); Collaborative Decision Log; Business Rules Registry; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board; North/South Runway Meter; East/West Apron Sensor; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Weather Ingest Gateway; Flight Data Exchange (Flight Intent Message, realized times); Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Sector Load Monitor; Common Situation Display; Contingency Operations Console; Arrival Regulation Console; Post Operations Report; Airport Capacity Plan. Silverpine grants emergency access only after IAS records incident reference/expiry. Actors: Airline Operations Coordinator (TOBT=Target Off Block Time) and Aircraft Operator Representative submit/update Flight Intent Messages, challenge via Decision Log; Regional Flow Manager; Slot Coordinator (SAE, Portal, Rules); Data Governance Steward (trains on data quality, privacy, Ledger); Meteorology Briefing Officer; Airport Duty Manager (revises Capacity Plan, mode changes); Tower Supervisor; controllers; System Support Engineer (trains superusers on Contingency Console); Ramp Control Lead (trains ramp personnel; Board never replaces visual checks, radio, local safety); Ground Handling Dispatcher (trains handlers on Planner); Network Operations Liaison, Airspace Sector Planner (Sector Load Monitor); Emergency Response Coordinator (command authority preserved); Deicing Coordinator (seasonal). Training: initial classroom, supervised practice, Briefing Room scenarios, shadowing before independent use; recurrent annually and after major changes to Platform/DPS/CAM/FDE; realistic simulations. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase; Slot Compliance; Contingency Fallback (ADM declares after consulting RFM).

New part:
S881: Each exercise shall include participants from tower, ramp, airline operations, handling, airport operations, network coordination, meteorology, data governance, and system support functions when those functions are relevant to the scenario.
S882: Exercises shall cover transitions among Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, and Slot Compliance State.
S883: Simulation events shall require users to compare automated recommendations with local knowledge, document significant decisions in the Collaborative Decision Log, and explain departures from system proposals.
S884: Human factors safeguards shall include workload monitoring, clear alert prioritization, consistent terminology, confirmation steps for high impact actions, and protection against silent mode changes.
S885: Workstation layouts shall support rapid comparison between the Common Situation Display, Airport CDM Portal, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, and relevant advisory messages without forcing users to copy critical values manually.
S886: Training assessments shall verify that users can identify stale data, time synchronization problems, duplicate flights, conflicting constraints, and inappropriate automation reliance before such issues affect live operations.
S887: Post-exercise reviews shall use evidence from the Performance Analytics Warehouse and Audit Event Ledger to improve procedures, refine training materials, and confirm that human performance concerns are assigned to accountable owners.
S888: Deployment of the Regional Flow Platform shall proceed through phased increments that limit operational exposure while progressively adding airports, interfaces, and decision support functions.
S889: The first increment shall establish the core operational baseline for the Regional Flow Manager, Network Operations Liaison, Data Governance Steward, and System Support Engineer in a controlled production environment.
S890: This baseline shall include the Identity Access Service, Time Synchronization Service, Audit Event Ledger, Performance Analytics Warehouse, and Business Rules Registry before any airport is permitted to exchange operational data.
S891: Pilot airport selection shall favor locations with stable operational leadership, representative traffic complexity, available surface surveillance data, and demonstrated willingness to participate in joint procedure development.
S892: The initial pilot shall include one constrained primary airport and one less constrained regional airport so that both high-demand and routine operating patterns are exercised.
S893: Each candidate airport shall provide evidence that the Airport Duty Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airline Operations Coordinator, Ground Handling Dispatcher, and Aircraft Operator Representative have named accountable implementation contacts.
S894: Readiness Gate 1 shall confirm that governance, security approvals, user role definitions, operating hours, and support escalation paths are documented and accepted by local stakeholders.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
